severity: HIGH — the country tag is factually wrong and it is the ONLY eligibility signal on the row
title: National History Day (NHD)
current_qualifiers: NONE — no citizenship_restrictions, no residency_restrictions, no eligible_citizenships. The country array is the entire eligibility story this row tells.
finding: WRONG. National History Day runs official affiliates OUTSIDE the United States. A student in Shanghai, Seoul or Singapore can compete through an official NHD affiliate, and this row tells ORYN they cannot.

us_overseas_affiliates_also_present.note: US Department of Defense Education Activity schools — US schools located overseas

us_overseas_affiliates_also_present.sponsoring_institution: American Samoa Department of Education, Office of Curriculum & Instruction

distinction_that_matters: Two different things are being conflated by the single 'United States' tag. (a) US TERRITORIES and DoDEA schools — arguably covered by a loose reading of 'United States'. (b) NHD China, NHD Korea and NHD International — affiliates in CHINA, SOUTH KOREA and SINGAPORE, which no reading of 'United States' covers. Only (b) makes the tag flatly wrong, and (b) is confirmed.
evidence: nhd.org's own affiliate directory (5 pages, '58 total posts'). NHD China appears on page 1 with its sponsoring institution and 2026 contest date; NHD International (Singapore) on page 2; NHD Korea on page 3; Guam on page 4; American Samoa on page 5; Northern Mariana Islands and NHD DODEA Atlantic also listed.
honest_limit: The affiliate pages state WHERE contests are held and WHO sponsors them. They do NOT state student-level eligibility — every affiliate page returned NOT STATED on which students may take part. So I can prove affiliates exist outside the US; I CANNOT prove from these pages that any student of any nationality may enter one. Do not replace one over-confident claim with another.
interesting_contrast: Regeneron STS explicitly EXCLUDES non-US-citizens attending American schools abroad. NHD's international affiliates ARE hosted at exactly such schools (Concordia Shanghai, Seoul International, Singapore American). Two US-headquartered competitions appear to treat the American-school-abroad student oppositely — which is precisely why this cannot be normalised into a shared country representation.
proposed_action: Do NOT simply append China/South Korea/Singapore to eligible_countries — that would assert student-level eligibility I have not established. Instead: (a) record that entry is via an NHD-affiliated contest and that affiliates exist outside the US, (b) point to the affiliate directory as the authoritative per-location check, (c) at minimum remove the bare ['United States'] tag's implied exclusivity, since it is the row's only eligibility signal and it is demonstrably too narrow.
unresolved: Student-level citizenship/residency rules for NHD — not stated on any affiliate page retrieved. Needs the contest rule book.

Eligibility 'high-achieving high school seniors with financial need'. CITIZENSHIP: **NOT STATED** on the programme page — so the ['United States'] tag is unverified rather than proven wrong.

audit_method_note: Query used: 'United States' = any(eligible_countries) AND citizenship_restrictions blank AND residency_restrictions blank AND eligible_citizenships empty. That is the right query for CEO's question, but the Ashoka row shows it needs a second filter — a multi-country array is evidence that someone DID determine eligibility, so single-element arrays are the higher-yield target.
